narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 36.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. Although a good outcome was still more likely than not, this estimate is above the risk limit the bank uses for approval, so your application did not pass.

The strongest factor was your checking account status, with a balance in the 0–200 DM range. This was the most influential feature and it pushed the decision toward bad credit. Among approved applicants, most had no checking-account issue, and only about one in five had a balance in your range. Two factors worked in your favor but were not enough to outweigh that concern. Your one year at your present residence was the second most important feature and reduced the perceived risk in your case. Your requested loan term of 12 months was third most important and also reduced risk, since it is shorter than the average approved term of about 19 months.

To improve your chances next time, focus first on your checking account: avoid overdrafts, build a steadier balance, and keep records showing regular income. Ask the bank what account balance or history it expects, correct any inaccurate account information, and consider reapplying once your account status is stronger. Keeping a shorter loan term while improving your account history is your best next step.
